lesson.summary: A derived set protects ADDITIONS and cannot detect a member LEAVING; pin as well as derive
lesson.synthesized_rule: Deriving a list of sites/members by grepping for a property is the right defence against a new member that lacks the property. It is NO defence against an existing member silently dropping out, because a member that stops matching stops being in the set -- and its per-member checks leave with it. A count floor does not help either: a new member satisfies the count. Union a derived sweep with an explicit pinned set and assert derived-is-a-superset-of-pinned, so a dropout fails loudly as a removal.
